articles.title: Driver arrested after stolen vehicle recovered on Milnrow Road in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: A driver has been arrested after Rochdale neighbourhood officers stopped a vehicle on Milnrow Road that police say had been reported stolen from North Wales.
articles.content_html:
A driver has been arrested after Greater Manchester Police officers recovered a vehicle on Milnrow Road in Rochdale which police say had been reported stolen from North Wales.

According to Rochdale GMP, PC Maestro and PCSO Davies from the neighbourhood team sighted the vehicle on Milnrow Road during the afternoon of Saturday, August 15.

Police checks on the vehicle showed it had been recorded as stolen from North Wales.

The driver was arrested and the vehicle was seized by officers.

Greater Manchester Police said the investigation remains ongoing. No further details about the driver, the circumstances of the alleged theft or any potential charges had been released at the time of publication.

articles.title: Man Banned from Keeping Animals for 15 Years After Neglecting Dog in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Paul Lewis Dawson from Burnley has received a 15-year ban on owning animals after admitting to neglecting his dog, Kano, in a Rochdale property. The case was brought to light following an RSPCA investigation.
articles.content_html:
BREAKING NEWS — LIVE

Live updates, newest first.

10:20, 14 August 2026

Paul Lewis Dawson from Burnley has received a 15-year ban on owning animals after admitting to neglecting his dog, Kano, in a Rochdale property. The case was brought to light following an RSPCA investigation.

A man from Burnley has been sentenced to a 22-week suspended prison sentence and banned from keeping animals for 15 years after admitting to multiple animal welfare offences. Paul Lewis Dawson, residing on Brownside Road, was prosecuted following an investigation by the RSPCA regarding the condition of his bull breed dog, Kano, at an address on Alice Street in Rochdale.

The RSPCA began their investigation on 6 August last year after receiving concerns from the public about the dog's welfare. RSPCA inspector Beth Fazackerley and Animal Rescue Officer Francesca Iraci visited the property and observed Kano through the keyhole, noting his emaciated state. Despite attempts to contact Dawson, they received no response, prompting them to push wet dog food through the letterbox, which Kano consumed.

After obtaining a warrant with Greater Manchester Police, the officers returned to the property later that evening. Upon entry, Inspector Fazackerley described Kano's condition as alarming. The dog struggled to walk and exhibited signs of severe neglect, including visible ribs and hip bones, skin infections, and a significant flea infestation. The inspector noted that she had never seen fleas in such large clumps before.

Dawson pleaded guilty to three charges of failing to provide a suitable diet, adequate veterinary care, and a suitable living environment for Kano at Tameside Magistrates’ Court on 31 July. The case highlights the importance of reporting animal welfare concerns and the role of the RSPCA in investigating such matters.

articles.title: Service Changes on Rochdale Line Due to Planned Works
articles.excerpt: Planned works on the Rochdale line will result in service changes from 15 to 28 August, with bus replacements in place for affected stops.
articles.content_html:
Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has announced that planned works will take place on the Rochdale line from Saturday 15 August until Friday 28 August, resulting in significant service changes. During this period, a bus replacement service will operate between affected stops to accommodate passengers.

Additionally, on Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August, works will occur in Manchester city centre, specifically at Manchester Town Hall. Consequently, no trams will operate via Exchange Square, with services on the East Didsbury and Trafford Centre lines rerouted via Market Street and Shudehill instead.

Passengers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly, as these disruptions may affect travel times. TfGM encourages those needing assistance or further information to contact their customer service help point or call the Metrolink contact centre at 0161 244 1000, available from 7am to 8pm on weekdays and 8am to 8pm on weekends and bank holidays.

In addition to the Rochdale line works, essential improvement works will take place at Prestwich Metrolink stop from Monday 18 May to Wednesday 19 August. While tram services will not be affected, an increased presence of staff is expected at this stop during this time.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC Netball launched as Rochdale Netball Club joins Dale family
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Netball Club is becoming Rochdale AFC Netball in a new partnership with Rochdale AFC and its Community Trust, bringing nearly 200 weekly players into the club's wider sporting family.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Netball Club is joining the Rochdale AFC family under a new identity as Rochdale AFC Netball, in a partnership designed to grow the sport and create more opportunities for women, girls and the wider community across the borough.

The agreement brings together Rochdale AFC, Rochdale AFC Community Trust and one of the borough's established community sports clubs under the wider 'Our Teams' banner.

Rochdale Netball Club currently runs teams from under-six level through to seniors, with nearly 200 players taking to the court each week. Under the new Rochdale AFC Netball identity, the organisations hope to strengthen the route from school participation into junior and adult club netball while also expanding opportunities in coaching, volunteering and leadership.

The partnership is expected to support new programmes in schools, holiday provision, health and wellbeing and volunteer development. The shared Rochdale AFC identity could also open up additional opportunities for sponsorship, commercial support, community events and promotion through the football club.

Amy Williams, Chair of Rochdale AFC Netball, described the move as a fantastic opportunity for both the club and the sport locally, saying joining the Rochdale AFC family would provide a stronger platform to grow the game and inspire more women and girls to become involved.

Rochdale AFC chief executive Laura Thomas, herself a former netball player, said she was thrilled to welcome the club into the wider Rochdale AFC family and stressed that the club's ambition to build a thriving community extends beyond football.

Ryan Bradley, Community Director at Rochdale AFC Community Trust, said the football club, charity and netball club shared common values and could combine their respective strengths. He said bringing the organisations together under one brand would raise netball's profile in Rochdale and strengthen support for volunteers, coaches, community outreach and school work.

Rochdale AFC Netball will be based at Edgar Wood. The Community Trust also pointed to plans for the Community Football and Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee, saying the geographical proximity of the projects made closer cooperation a natural step.

The move follows a wider trend in British sport in which professional football and rugby clubs have partnered with netball organisations to increase visibility, participation and long-term sustainability. In Rochdale, the organisations say their approach will remain community focused and open to people of all ages.

Further information about Rochdale AFC Netball teams, programmes and opportunities to get involved is expected to be announced in due course.

articles.title: WellMental UK hosts first men's mental health fitness session in Heywood
articles.excerpt: WellMental UK held its first session in Heywood on Friday evening, combining fitness, food and conversation to support men's mental health.
articles.content_html:
WellMental UK hosted its first men's mental health fitness session in Heywood on Friday evening, bringing local men together for exercise, food and conversation.

The session took place at Unit4 Fitness and began with a group workout before moving into a relaxed social evening. Attendees shared a curry, spent time together and were encouraged to talk openly in an informal setting.

Organisers said it was encouraging to see those attending getting involved, supporting one another and making the most of the opportunity to spend time together.

The event was designed to combine physical activity with peer support and conversation, creating a space where men could connect without the pressure of a formal clinical environment.

WellMental UK thanked everyone who attended and helped make the first Heywood session a success.

The evening marked the beginning of the group's activity in Heywood, with the first session focused on building community, encouraging openness and using fitness as a way to bring people together.

articles.title: LIVE: Woman arrested on suspicion of murder after 31-year-old man dies in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: A 37-year-old woman has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a 31-year-old man died at an address in Rochdale.
articles.content_html:
BREAKING NEWS — LIVE

14:04, 13 August 2026 — A murder investigation has been launched after a 31-year-old man died at an address in Rochdale.

Emergency services were called to a property on Great Howarth shortly before 7.40pm on Tuesday 11 August. A man was found unresponsive inside the address. Paramedics attempted to save him, but he was pronounced dead a short time later.

A 37-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of murder as officers began enquiries into the circumstances surrounding the death. An arrest is not a finding of guilt, and the investigation remains at an early stage.

Police had not released the man's identity in the information available to Rochdale Daily when this report was first published. This is a developing story and verified updates will be added here with timestamps as they are confirmed.

The case concerns an address on Great Howarth in Rochdale.

articles.title: M62 Reopens After Sheep Incident Between J21 Rochdale and J23 Huddersfield
articles.excerpt: The M62 has reopened in both directions after delays caused by sheep on the motorway. National Highways confirmed the situation has been resolved, but residual delays remain.
articles.content_html:
The M62 motorway has reopened in both directions between Junction 21 (Rochdale) and Junction 23 (Huddersfield) following an incident involving sheep on the carriageway. National Highways confirmed that the sheep have been secured and removed from the area, allowing traffic to resume.

The incident caused significant delays, with reports of residual congestion of up to 90 minutes and approximately seven miles of tailbacks on the approach to the affected junctions. Motorists are advised to remain cautious as traffic gradually returns to normal.

The delays began earlier in the day when the sheep were spotted wandering on the motorway, prompting emergency services to respond and secure the area. The quick action by authorities ensured that the situation was resolved without any reported injuries or accidents.

Drivers are encouraged to check traffic updates before setting out, as some residual delays may still be experienced. National Highways has advised all motorists to have a safe onward journey as the situation stabilises.

articles.excerpt: Tram services between Victoria and Rochdale Town Centre are suspended as improvement works are carried out. A replacement bus service is in operation for affected passengers until further notice.

Tram improvement works are currently taking place on the Rochdale Line, resulting in the suspension of all tram services between Victoria and Rochdale Town Centre. This disruption began on 15 August 2026 and will continue until the completion of the works, with no specified end date provided.

In response to the service interruption, a replacement bus service has been implemented, which will call at all affected tram stops. Passengers are advised to check local transport updates for further information regarding the bus service and any changes to the timetable.

Additionally, from 17 to 28 August, there will be further disruptions as no trams will run between Oldham Mumps and Rochdale Town Centre. This phase of repair work is necessary following a landslip at Derker in 2024, and it aims to remove the temporary speed restrictions currently in place.

Local residents and commuters are encouraged to plan their journeys accordingly and to remain updated on the ongoing improvements and their impact on tram services.

events.title: The Black Dyke Band at Rochdale Town Hall 2027
events.excerpt: In 1871 The Black Dyke Band performed at the original opening ceremony for Rochdale Town Hall. Since the post refurbishment of the Town Hall, the band have since gone on to perform every year bringing the best of brass band quality for all to enjoy. Join them again in 2027. Rochdale, Town Hall, The Esplanade, Rochdale
